- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a downward correction of 2–5% for the next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.3) in the last 3–5 days, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for potential reversal or volatility.
- Model consistently underestimates in the first 3–5 days of a new sentiment cycle; apply a 1–2% upward bias for early forecast horizon.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.5–0.75), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to match sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent highs; apply a 3–5% downward adjustment if recent 7-day average is above 70.00.
